subNote: 질문 영어 표시(실제 시험에서는 표시되지 않아요)

open.t: Hi, I'm Eva. I'll be asking you some questions today. Please answer as completely as you can.

close.t: Thank you. That's the end of the interview.

q1.q: Let's start the interview now. Tell me something about yourself.
model: Hi, my name is Minjun, and I'm a university student in Seoul. I'm majoring in business, and I'm in my third year. I live with my parents and my younger sister in an apartment near the Han River. In my free time, I like listening to music and riding my bike along the river. I'm a pretty outgoing person, so I enjoy meeting new people. After I graduate, I hope to work for an international company, so I'm trying hard to improve my English.
points: 이름 → 하는 일 → 사는 곳 → 취미 → 앞으로의 목표

q2.q: You indicated in the survey that you listen to music. What kind of music do you like? Who are some of your favorite singers or bands?
q2.ja: 어떤 음악을 좋아하나요? 좋아하는 가수나 밴드는?
model: I listen to all kinds of music, but my favorite is K-pop and some indie rock. I especially like a band called Day6, because their songs have really meaningful lyrics, and they actually play their own instruments. When I'm tired, their songs give me energy. I also listen to some old pop songs that my parents used to play when I was a kid, so I guess my taste is pretty mixed.

q3.q: When and where do you usually listen to music? Describe a typical day when you listen to music.
q3.ja: 보통 언제, 어디에서 음악을 듣나요? 하루의 흐름을 설명해 주세요.
model: I usually listen to music on my way to school. It takes about forty minutes by subway, so I put on my earphones as soon as I leave home. In the afternoon, I listen to calm music while I'm studying at the library. Then at night, before I go to bed, I listen to something relaxing. So basically, music is with me all day long.

q4.q: Tell me about a memorable experience related to music, such as a concert you went to. What happened, and why was it so memorable?
q4.ja: 음악과 관련된 기억에 남는 경험을 말해 주세요.
model: Last summer, I went to an outdoor music festival with my friends. It was really hot, and we waited in line for almost two hours. But when my favorite band came on stage, everyone started singing along, and I totally forgot about the heat. Then suddenly it started to rain, but nobody left. We just kept dancing in the rain. It was one of the best days of my life.
points: 언제 → 무슨 일 → 왜 기억에 남는지

q5.q: You said that you ride a bicycle. Where do you usually go cycling? Describe the place for me.
q5.ja: 보통 어디에서 자전거를 타나요? 그곳을 묘사해 주세요.
model: I usually ride along the Han River. There's a long bike path that goes all the way across the city. On one side, you can see the river, and on the other side, there are parks and convenience stores. In the evening, the bridges light up, and the view is really beautiful. There are always a lot of people jogging or having picnics, so it feels lively.

q6.q: What do you usually do to get ready before you go cycling? Tell me about your routine.
q6.ja: 자전거를 타기 전에 보통 무엇을 하나요?
model: Before I go, I check the weather first, because riding in the rain is dangerous. Then I check the tires and the brakes. I always wear a helmet and bring a bottle of water. I also make a playlist for the ride. Usually I leave around six in the evening, when it's not too hot, and ride for about an hour.

q7.q: Tell me about a time when something unexpected happened while you were cycling. What happened, and how did you deal with it?
q7.ja: 자전거를 타다가 예상치 못한 일이 있었던 경험은?
model: One time, I got a flat tire when I was really far from home. I didn't have any tools, and my phone battery was almost dead. I was kind of panicking, but luckily, another cyclist stopped and helped me. He had a repair kit and fixed it in ten minutes. Since then, I always carry a small repair kit with me.
points: 문제 → 해결 → 그 후 달라진 점

q8.q: I'd like to give you a situation and ask you to act it out. You are planning a trip to Jeju Island and want to book a hotel. Call the hotel and ask three or four questions about the rooms.
q8.ja: 롤플레이: 제주도 호텔에 전화해서 객실에 대해 3~4가지 질문하기
model: Hi, I'm calling because I'd like to book a room for next weekend. First, do you have any double rooms available from Friday to Sunday? And how much is it per night? Also, is breakfast included in the price? One more thing, do you have a room with an ocean view? And finally, is there free parking at the hotel? Thank you so much.
points: Do you have … / Is … included? / How much …?

q9.q: I'm sorry, but there is a problem I need you to resolve. When you arrive at the hotel, the staff says your reservation is not in the system. Explain the situation and offer two or three alternatives to solve the problem.
q9.ja: 롤플레이: 예약이 안 되어 있다는 문제를 설명하고 해결책 2~3가지 제안하기
model: Hi, I booked a double room for two nights last week, but you're saying my reservation isn't in the system. I have the confirmation email right here on my phone. Could you check again with my phone number? If there's really no record, could you give me a similar room at the same price? Or if the hotel is full, could you help me find another hotel nearby? I'd really appreciate your help.

q10.q: Have you ever had a problem with a reservation, like at a hotel or a restaurant? Tell me what happened and how you solved it.
q10.ja: 예약과 관련해 문제가 있었던 경험이 있나요?
model: Yes, it happened last year on my birthday. I booked a table at an Italian restaurant, but when we arrived, they said they had no reservation for us. I showed them the text message, and the manager apologized. They didn't have a table at that moment, so they gave us free drinks while we waited for about twenty minutes. In the end, it was fine.

q11.q: Let's talk about something different. How do people recycle in your country? Describe the recycling system.
q11.ja: 돌발 주제: 한국의 재활용 방법을 설명해 주세요.
model: In Korea, recycling is really strict. We have to separate plastic, paper, cans and glass, and food waste goes in a special bag. In my apartment, there's a recycling area, and we can take things out only on certain days of the week. If you don't separate things properly, you can get a fine. It's a bit annoying, but I think it's a good system.

q12.q: How has recycling changed compared to the past? Tell me about any changes you have noticed.
model: When I was a kid, people didn't separate their trash that much. Now, everyone is much more careful. For example, these days, we have to remove the labels from plastic bottles before we throw them away. Also, a lot of cafés don't give out plastic straws anymore. I think people have become more aware of environmental problems.

model: Hi, my name is Minjun, and I'm a university student in Seoul. I'm majoring in business, and I'm in my third year. I live with my parents and my younger sister in an apartment near the Han River. In my free time, I like listening to music and riding my bike along the river. I'm a pretty outgoing person, so I enjoy meeting new people. After I graduate, I hope to work for an international company, so I'm trying hard to improve my English.
points: 이름 → 하는 일 → 사는 곳 → 취미 → 앞으로의 목표

q2.q: In the survey, you indicated that you like watching movies. What kinds of movies do you like, and why?
model: I like action movies and also animated movies. Action movies are exciting, and they help me forget about stress. Animated movies, especially Japanese ones, have really beautiful scenes and warm stories. I usually watch movies on weekends. If a movie gets good reviews, I go to the theater, but most of the time I watch them at home.

q3.q: Describe what you usually do when you go to the movies, from the beginning to the end.
q3.ja: 영화를 보러 갈 때 보통 무엇을 하나요? 처음부터 끝까지 설명해 주세요.
model: First, I check the reviews online and book tickets with an app. I usually go with my best friend. We meet about thirty minutes early and buy popcorn and drinks. After the movie, we go to a café and talk about the story. Sometimes we disagree about the ending, and that's actually the most fun part.

q4.q: Tell me about the most memorable movie you have ever seen. What was it about, and why do you remember it?
q4.ja: 가장 기억에 남는 영화는? 왜 기억에 남나요?
model: The most memorable movie for me is a documentary about a pilot who flew around the world in a small plane. I watched it with my father when I was in high school. There were so many problems during the trip, but she never gave up. After watching it, I started to think more seriously about my dreams. That's why I still remember it.

q5.q: You said that you go to parks. Describe a park you often go to. What does it look like?
model: There's a big park near my house called Olympic Park. It has huge lawns, a lake and a lot of sculptures. In the spring, there are cherry blossoms everywhere, and in the fall, the trees turn yellow and red. There are walking trails and bike paths, and on weekends, there are sometimes concerts. It's my favorite place to relax.

q6.q: What do you usually do when you go to the park? Tell me about a typical visit.
model: Usually I go there on Sunday mornings. I walk around the lake for about an hour while listening to a podcast. Then I sit on a bench and read a book or just watch people. Sometimes I meet my friends there, and we play badminton. On the way home, I usually stop at a bakery and buy some bread.

q7.q: Tell me about a special day you had at a park. What happened?
q7.ja: 공원에서 있었던 특별한 하루를 말해 주세요.
model: Last spring, my family had a picnic in the park to celebrate my grandmother's seventieth birthday. We prepared lots of food, and my sister and I made a cake. While we were eating, a street musician started playing near us, and he even played a birthday song for my grandmother. She was so happy that she cried a little. I'll never forget that day.

q8.q: Let me give you a situation to act out. You want to buy a new smartphone. Go to an electronics store and ask the clerk three or four questions about the phone you want.
model: Hi, I'm looking for a new smartphone. I'm interested in this model. How long does the battery last? And how much storage does it have? Also, does it come in other colors, like blue or green? Lastly, is there any discount if I trade in my old phone? Thanks for your help.
points: Is there …? / Does it …? / How long …?

q9.q: I'm sorry, but there is a problem. After you bought the phone, you found out that it doesn't charge. Call the store, explain the problem, and suggest two or three ways to solve it.
q9.ja: 롤플레이: 산 휴대폰이 충전되지 않는 문제를 설명하고 해결책 제안하기
model: Hello, I bought a smartphone at your store yesterday, but it won't charge at all. I tried a different cable and charger, but it still doesn't work. Could I exchange it for a new one? If you don't have the same model in stock, could I get a refund? Or, if you can repair it within two or three days, that would be okay too. Please let me know what's possible.

q10.q: Have you ever bought something that didn't work properly? Tell me what happened and what you did about it.
q10.ja: 산 물건이 제대로 작동하지 않았던 경험은?
model: Yes, I once bought wireless earphones online, and the right one didn't make any sound. I contacted the seller and sent a video showing the problem. They apologized and sent me a new pair, but it took almost two weeks. Since then, I prefer to buy electronics at a store, so I can exchange them right away.

q11.q: Let's talk about the weather. Describe the seasons in your country. What is the weather like in each season?
q11.ja: 돌발 주제: 한국의 계절과 날씨를 설명해 주세요.
model: Korea has four distinct seasons. Spring is warm, and flowers bloom everywhere, but there's a lot of fine dust. Summer is hot and humid, and we have a rainy season in July. Fall is my favorite season, because the sky is clear and the weather is cool. Winter is very cold and dry, and sometimes it snows.

q12.q: How has the weather in your country changed compared to when you were a child?
q12.ja: 어렸을 때와 비교해 날씨는 어떻게 바뀌었나요?
model: I think summers have become much hotter. When I was a kid, we didn't use the air conditioner that often, but now we can't live without it. Also, spring and fall feel shorter than before. It seems like it goes from winter to summer very quickly. I think climate change is the reason.

q2.q: You indicated in the survey that you like to travel in your country. Tell me about a place in Korea that you like to visit. What is it like?
model: One of my favorite places is Gangneung, on the east coast. It takes about two hours from Seoul by KTX. There's a long, beautiful beach, and the water is really clear. Near the beach, there's a street full of coffee shops, so people call it a coffee town. I love sitting by the window of a café and just looking at the sea. It's the perfect place to relax.

q3.q: What do you usually do to prepare for a trip? Tell me everything you do, from the beginning to the end.
q3.ja: 여행 준비를 할 때 보통 무엇을 하나요?
model: First, I decide where to go with my friends. Then we book train tickets and a guesthouse online, usually a few weeks before the trip. After that, I search for good restaurants and make a simple plan, but not too detailed. The night before the trip, I pack my bag. I always bring a portable charger, a light jacket and comfortable shoes.

q4.q: Tell me about a trip that didn't go as planned. What happened, and how did you handle it?
q4.ja: 계획대로 되지 않았던 여행 경험을 말해 주세요.
model: Last year, I went to Busan with my friends, but a typhoon came on the second day. All the outdoor plans were canceled, and we were stuck in our guesthouse. At first, we were really disappointed. But then we found a small board game café nearby and spent the whole afternoon there. We also tried a famous pork soup restaurant. In the end, it became one of our funniest trips.
points: 문제 → 해결 → 그 후 느낀 점

q5.q: You said that you go to coffee shops. Describe a coffee shop you often go to. What does it look like?
model: There's a small café near my school that I go to almost every day. It's on the second floor, so you can see the street through big windows. The walls are white, and there are a lot of plants everywhere. They play calm jazz music, so it's a nice place to study. My favorite drink there is an iced vanilla latte.

q6.q: What do you usually do when you go to a coffee shop? Tell me about a typical visit.
model: I usually go in the afternoon after my classes. First, I order a drink and find a seat near an outlet. Then I open my laptop and do my assignments for about two hours. Sometimes my friends join me, and we take a break and chat. Before I leave, I usually buy a piece of cake to take home.

q7.q: Tell me about a memorable experience you had at a coffee shop.
q7.ja: 카페에서 기억에 남는 경험을 말해 주세요.
model: One day, I was studying at a café when I spilled my coffee all over my laptop. I panicked, but the staff came right away with lots of tissues and helped me clean it. Luckily, the laptop still worked. They even gave me a new coffee for free. Since then, I always put my drink far away from my laptop, and I go to that café even more often.
points: 문제 → 해결 → 그 후 달라진 점

q8.q: I'd like to give you a situation and ask you to act it out. You want to join a fitness center near your home. Call the fitness center and ask three or four questions to get the information you need.
model: Hi, I'm thinking about joining your fitness center, so I have a few questions. First, what are your opening hours on weekends? Also, how much is a monthly membership? Is there a discount if I sign up for three months? And do you offer any group classes, like yoga or spinning? Lastly, is there a shower room and lockers? Thanks a lot.

q9.q: I'm sorry, but there is a problem I need you to resolve. You signed up for a yoga class, but when you arrive, you find out that the class has been canceled. Talk to the staff, explain the situation and suggest two or three alternatives.
q9.ja: 롤플레이: 요가 수업이 취소된 문제를 설명하고 대안 2~3가지 제시하기
model: Hi, I came for the seven o'clock yoga class, but I just heard it's been canceled. I didn't get any message about it, and I came straight from work. Could I join another yoga class tonight or tomorrow instead? If that's not possible, could you add one extra class to my membership? Or maybe I could get a discount for this month. Please let me know.

q10.q: Have you ever had a problem with a class or an event that was canceled at the last minute? What happened, and how did you deal with it?
q10.ja: 수업이나 행사가 갑자기 취소된 경험이 있나요?
model: Yes, last spring my friends and I bought tickets for an outdoor concert, but it was canceled two hours before it started because of heavy rain. We were already on the way, so we were really upset. We got a full refund a few days later. Instead of going home, we went to a nearby restaurant and listened to the band's songs together. It wasn't the same, but it was still fun.

q11.q: Let's talk about something different. What is public transportation like in your country? Describe the buses and subways.
q11.ja: 돌발 주제: 한국의 대중교통을 묘사해 주세요.
model: Public transportation in Korea is really convenient. In Seoul, the subway goes almost everywhere, and trains come every few minutes. Buses are color-coded, so it's easy to know where they're going. You can use one transportation card for both buses and the subway, and you get a discount when you transfer. It's also clean and safe, even late at night.

q12.q: How has public transportation changed compared to the past? Tell me about the changes you have noticed.
model: When I was little, I had to pay with cash on the bus, and there was no information about when the bus would come. These days, there are screens at bus stops that show the arrival time, and I can check everything on my phone. Many buses are now electric, so they're quieter and cleaner. I think it's become much more comfortable.

q2.q: You indicated in the survey that you like cooking. What kind of food do you like to cook? Describe a dish you are good at.
model: I really enjoy cooking Korean food, and my best dish is kimchi fried rice. It's simple, but it tastes amazing. I fry kimchi with some pork and green onions, then add rice and a little gochujang. At the end, I put a fried egg on top and sprinkle some sesame seeds. It's my go-to meal when I'm hungry late at night.

q3.q: Tell me about the steps you usually take when you cook a meal at home, from shopping to cleaning up.
q3.ja: 집에서 요리할 때의 과정을 처음부터 끝까지 말해 주세요.
model: First, I check what's in the fridge and make a short list. Then I go to the supermarket near my apartment to buy fresh vegetables and meat. When I get home, I wash and cut everything before I start cooking, so it goes smoothly. After I eat, I wash the dishes right away and wipe the kitchen counter. I don't like leaving a mess.

q4.q: Tell me about a time when you cooked something special for other people. What happened?
q4.ja: 다른 사람들을 위해 특별한 요리를 했던 경험을 말해 주세요.
model: Last year, I made a birthday dinner for my mom. I wanted to surprise her, so I cooked seaweed soup, japchae and grilled fish while she was out. I'd never made japchae before, so I watched a video three times. The noodles got a little too soft, but my mom said it was the best birthday dinner ever. I felt really proud.

q5.q: You said that you go to see performances. Tell me about a theater or concert hall you have been to. What was it like?
model: I've been to a concert hall in the Olympic Park in Seoul a few times. It's a huge round building, and it can hold thousands of people. Inside, the stage is really big, and there are giant screens on both sides, so you can see the performers even from the back. Outside, there's a big park, so people often take pictures before the show.

q6.q: What do you usually do before and after you watch a performance?
q6.ja: 공연을 보기 전과 후에 보통 무엇을 하나요?
model: Before the show, I usually meet my friends and have dinner nearby. We arrive at the hall about thirty minutes early to buy some merchandise and find our seats. After the show, we always go to a café and talk about our favorite moments. Then I post a few pictures on social media before I go to bed.

q7.q: Tell me about the most memorable performance you have ever seen.
q7.ja: 가장 기억에 남는 공연을 말해 주세요.
model: The most memorable one was a musical I saw with my sister for her graduation. We got seats in the second row, so we could see the actors' faces clearly. In the last scene, the main actor sang a song about following your dreams, and my sister started crying. Afterward, we waited outside and got the actor's autograph. It was a really special day for both of us.

q8.q: I'd like to give you a situation and ask you to act it out. You want to buy a new smartphone. Go to a store and ask the salesperson three or four questions about the phone you want.
model: Hi, I'm looking for a new smartphone. Could you tell me about this model? First, how long does the battery last? And how good is the camera, especially at night? I'd also like to know if it comes in other colors. One more thing, is there any discount if I trade in my old phone? Thank you.

q9.q: I'm sorry, but there is a problem I need you to resolve. A few days after you bought the phone, the screen stopped working. Go to the store, explain the problem and suggest two or three ways to solve it.
q9.ja: 롤플레이: 산 지 며칠 된 휴대폰 화면이 고장 난 문제를 해결하기
model: Hi, I bought this phone here three days ago, but the screen suddenly stopped working this morning. I didn't drop it or get it wet. I have the receipt with me. Could you exchange it for a new one? If you don't have the same model in stock, could you give me a full refund? Or at least, could you lend me a phone while it's being repaired?

q10.q: Have you ever bought something that turned out to be broken or different from what you expected? Tell me what happened.
q10.ja: 산 물건이 고장 났거나 기대와 달랐던 경험이 있나요?
model: Yes, I once ordered a jacket online, but when it arrived, it was much smaller than the size on the website. I contacted the seller and sent them pictures. They apologized and told me to send it back for free. A week later, I got the right size. Since then, I always read the reviews about sizes before I buy clothes online.

q11.q: Let's talk about something different. How do people in your country usually use banks? Describe what people do at the bank.
q11.ja: 돌발 주제: 한국 사람들은 은행을 어떻게 이용하나요?
model: These days, most people in Korea use banking apps on their phones. You can send money to friends in a few seconds, pay bills and even open an account without visiting a bank. People still go to the bank for more complicated things, like getting a loan. Older people also visit the bank more often, because they're more comfortable talking to staff in person.

q12.q: How has banking changed over the years? Tell me about the changes you have noticed.
model: When I was a child, my parents had to wait in line at the bank for a long time, and they kept a paper bankbook. Now, almost everything can be done on a phone, and many bank branches have closed. Cash is used much less, too. It's very convenient, but I think it can be difficult for elderly people who aren't used to smartphones.

q1.q: Let's start the interview now. Tell me something about yourself.
model: Hi, my name is Minjun, and I'm a university student in Seoul. I'm majoring in business, and I'm in my third year. I live with my parents and my younger sister in an apartment near the Han River. In my free time, I like listening to music and riding my bike along the river. I'm a pretty outgoing person, so I enjoy meeting new people. After I graduate, I hope to work for an international company, so I'm trying hard to improve my English.
points: 이름 → 하는 일 → 사는 곳 → 취미 → 앞으로의 목표

q2.q: You indicated in the survey that you go jogging. Where do you usually jog? Describe the place.
model: I usually jog in a park near my apartment. There's a running track that goes around a small lake, and it's about two kilometers long. There are tall trees along the track, so it's shady even in summer. In the morning, there are a lot of people walking their dogs or doing exercises. The air is fresh, and I can hear birds singing.

q3.q: When do you usually go jogging, and what do you do before and after? Tell me about your routine.
q3.ja: 조깅을 하기 전후의 루틴을 말해 주세요.
model: I usually jog three times a week, early in the morning before school. First, I drink a glass of water and do some stretching for about five minutes. Then I put on my earphones and run for about thirty minutes. After that, I walk slowly to cool down and stretch again. When I get home, I take a shower and eat a big breakfast.

q4.q: Tell me about a memorable experience you had while jogging or exercising.
q4.ja: 조깅이나 운동을 하다가 기억에 남는 경험을 말해 주세요.
model: Last spring, I ran my first ten-kilometer race with my older brother. At around the seventh kilometer, I got a cramp in my leg and almost gave up. My brother slowed down and ran with me until the end. We finished in just over an hour. It wasn't a great time, but crossing the finish line together was an amazing feeling.

q5.q: You said that you live in an apartment. Describe your home for me. What does it look like?
model: I live in an apartment on the twelfth floor with my family. When you open the door, there's a living room with a big sofa and a TV. The kitchen is right next to it. There are three bedrooms and two bathrooms. My room is small, but I love it because it has a big window, and I can see the mountains on a clear day.

q6.q: What do you usually do at home on weekends? Tell me about a typical weekend at home.
model: On Saturday mornings, I sleep in until about ten. Then I help my parents clean the house. I usually vacuum the living room and clean my own room. In the afternoon, I watch a movie or play games. On Sunday evenings, my family orders fried chicken and we watch a variety show together. It's my favorite time of the week.

q7.q: Tell me about a time when something went wrong at home, like a broken appliance. What happened, and how did you solve it?
q7.ja: 집에서 문제가 생겼던 경험을 말해 주세요.
model: Last summer, our air conditioner suddenly broke during a heat wave. It was so hot that we couldn't sleep. We called the repair service, but they said they couldn't come for four days because they were too busy. So we bought two electric fans and slept in the living room together, like camping. When the repairman finally came, it only took him twenty minutes to fix it.

q8.q: I'd like to give you a situation and ask you to act it out. A friend has invited you to a party. Call your friend and ask three or four questions about the party.
q8.ja: 롤플레이: 파티에 초대한 친구에게 전화해서 3~4가지 질문하기
model: Hey, thanks for inviting me to your party! I just have a few questions. What time does it start, and how long will it last? Also, who else is coming? Should I bring anything, like drinks or snacks? And is there parking near your place, or should I take the subway? Let me know. I'm really looking forward to it.

q9.q: I'm sorry, but there is a problem I need you to resolve. On the day of the party, you suddenly can't go. Call your friend, explain the situation and suggest two or three alternatives.
q9.ja: 롤플레이: 파티에 갈 수 없게 된 상황을 설명하고 대안 제시하기
model: Hi, it's me. I'm so sorry, but I can't come to your party tonight. My grandmother suddenly got sick, and I have to go to the hospital with my parents. I feel really bad about it. How about I take you out for dinner next weekend instead? Or I could come over tomorrow and help you clean up. Anyway, I'll send you a little present. Have a great time tonight.

q10.q: Have you ever had to cancel a plan with a friend at the last minute? Tell me what happened.
q10.ja: 친구와의 약속을 갑자기 취소해야 했던 경험이 있나요?
model: Yes, once I had to cancel a movie date with my best friend because I had a high fever. I called her an hour before we were supposed to meet. She wasn't angry at all. In fact, she came to my house with some porridge and medicine. We watched a movie on my laptop instead. That's when I realized what a good friend she is.

q11.q: Let's talk about something different. How do people in your country use the internet in their daily lives?
q11.ja: 돌발 주제: 한국 사람들은 일상에서 인터넷을 어떻게 사용하나요?
model: In Korea, the internet is part of almost everything. People use it to order food, shop, watch videos and even see a doctor online. The internet is really fast, and there's free Wi-Fi in most places, like subways and cafés. Many people also work or study online. Honestly, it's hard to imagine a day without the internet here.

q12.q: What are some problems caused by the internet? Tell me about a problem that people in your country are worried about.
model: One big problem is that people spend too much time on their phones. Some students stay up late watching videos and can't focus in class. Another problem is fake news. False information spreads very quickly online, and some people believe it without checking. I think schools should teach students how to use the internet in a healthy and smart way.
